title: Applying High-Reliability Organization (HRO) Principles to Multi-Agent AI Operations

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: operationalize HRO principles as agent interventions -> test failure rate reduction. The gap is that HRO principles are organizational/cultural and may not straightforwardly translate to prompt-level or design-level AI interventions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Surveying HRO principles and operationalizing them as prompts/design choices is conceptually accessible. Setting up a 3-agent system and running 20 tasks requires moderate framework familiarity. Within reach with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Five separate HRO principles each operationalized as different intervention types (prompt, design, monitoring) creates a wide scope. Even testing one principle on 20 tasks would be more focused. No clear single first milestone.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
